newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks halt slippage, closing firm.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks halt slippage, closing firm.

text.p: Caracas stocks halted a straight six-day slide, closing ahead on key trades in selected stocks, traders said, although the rise probably did not herald a new upward trend, they added.

"The market is going to continue to be erratic, rising some days and falling others," said Activalores broker Gonzalo Alonso. "But the fluctuations should not be great -- there's neither investors nor volume," he added.
The bolsa's leading 19-share index gained one percent to close at 6,263.57 points as 46 million shares traded worth 3.1 billion bolivars ($6.6 million).
Volume was boosted as nearly 33 million shares in Corimon B preferred shares exchanged hands, the stock closing up 0.25 bolivars at 9.00.
The B series stock represents capitalised debt, following a recent financial restructuring of the company, and its heavy trade signals a sell-off by former debt holders, traders said.
Among other widely held shares, utility Electricidad de Caracas gained 9.50 to close at 480.00, while telephone company CANTV gained 35.00 bolivars to end at 1905.00.
